trial_court: Court of learned Additional District Judge (Matrimonial Cases), Jammu
case_name: Sher Noble Manav And Ors vs State And Ors
facts_of_case: Petitioners are a legally wedded couple with strained relations. Petitioner No. 1 filed for divorce under Section 12 of J&K Hindu Marriage Act, while respondent No. 2 sought maintenance and restitution of conjugal rights. A compromise was reached to dissolve the marriage by mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: The High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime before exercising its power to quash criminal proceedings.
legal_principles.held: Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.

legal_principles.principle: The High Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak.
legal_principles.held: In this category of cases, High Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak

legal_principles.principle: The High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding.
legal_principles.held: In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding

keywords: Latin maxim: Actio non procedit contra debitorem
